clue.text: From a harbour see landing beach

indicators.note: see invites the solver to look inside the words 'From a harbour' for a run of letters spanning them

explanation.surface: A traveller looks out from a harbour towards a beach where boats land.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'From', all of 'a' and the start of 'harbour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha was one of the Normandy beaches where Allied troops came ashore on D-Day.

clue.text: German town, Essen, I'm developing

indicators.note: developing suggests something changing shape, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from the German city of Essen says they are growing as a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen is a town in Saxony, famous for its porcelain.

clue.text: Loathe grabbing seconds for speed

indicators.note: grabbing means the synonym for loathe holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to loathe is to hate

explanation.surface: Someone detests having to snatch extra helpings for the sake of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is a noun for hurry or quickness, a synonym of speed.

clue.text: Teacher cutting head off flower

indicators.note: cutting head off says the first letter of the teacher word is removed

parts.note: a schoolmaster, or master, is a teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher snips the top off a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden plant in bloom in late summer.

clue.text: Plaster-cast stationery item

indicators.note: cast can mean thrown about or formed anew, so the letters of plaster are rearranged

explanation.surface: An office gadget is moulded out of plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A stapler is a desk device for fastening papers, a common piece of office stationery.

clue.text: Arrive with extremity in the air

parts.note: an end is an extremity
something in the air is up, raised aloft

explanation.surface: Someone lands with one limb raised high.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up somewhere is an idiom for arriving there eventually.

clue.text: Flexible by having interior design

indicators.note: having interior means the word by takes the next piece as its contents

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose, a design

explanation.surface: Something is pliable because of how its inside was designed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bendy is an informal synonym for pliable, able to be bent easily.

clue.text: Helps when accepting wager

indicators.note: accepting means the word for when takes the next piece into it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A friend lends a hand by taking on a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, so abets matches helps.

clue.text: Took liquid from ditch opening — filthy!

indicators.note: the opening of ditch is its first letter

parts.note: rank means foul or filthy

explanation.surface: Someone drank from the mouth of a dirty ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: Drank is the past tense of drink, to take liquid in by mouth.

clue.text: Elvis' terrible sins

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of the singer's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: The rock and roll singer's awful wrongdoings are listed.
explanation.definitionFit: Evils are wicked acts, the same as sins.

clue.text: Verbal margin for paying guest

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the margin word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a border is a margin or edge

explanation.surface: A lodger is told off with a spoken warning at the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarder pays to live and eat in someone else's house, a lodger.

clue.text: Detective's posted for opposition

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, so detective's gives DI plus S
something posted has been sent

explanation.surface: A detective has been transferred elsewhere in the face of opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement with an official view, a form of opposition.

clue.text: Plant left out of bed at home

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A plant is left lying out of its flower bed at the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like flowers.

clue.text: A girl returns to find another

indicators.note: returns says the pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl comes back to search for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns A plus TINA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is another girl's name, so 'another' points to one more name after Tina.

clue.text: Strain of rattling one's tin

indicators.note: rattling suggests shaking up, so the letters of the following words are mixed

explanation.surface: The stress of hearing someone shake their collection tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is stress or tightness, a synonym of strain.

clue.text: Diver spills beer by first gate

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of gate is taken
spills suggests scattering, so the letters of beer are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer knocks over a drink beside the main entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places the gate's first letter G beside REBE, the rearranged beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a water bird that dives under water for fish.

clue.text: One extra, then two, for Land of Nod

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket
two such extras are byes

explanation.surface: Counting one, then two more, as a child drifts off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter without being hit; bye-byes is nursery talk for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The Land of Nod is a whimsical phrase for sleep, which children call bye-byes.

clue.text: Donkey goes round by canyon

indicators.note: goes round means the donkey word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey walks around next to a canyon.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a deep chasm, much like a canyon.

clue.text: Reads about challenges

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the letters of reads are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reads up on contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Dares are challenges to do something risky, as verbs or nouns.

clue.text: Drink interrupted by year of mawkishness

indicators.note: interrupted by means the drink word is broken by the next piece placed inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone's drinking is cut short by a year of sentimentality.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrup figuratively means cloying sentimentality, which is what mawkishness is.

clue.text: Books burnt regularly by naval officer

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken from the words before it

explanation.surface: A sailor burns books on a routine basis.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'Books burnt' are B, O, S, U, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun, or boatswain, is a ship's officer in charge of equipment and crew.

clue.text: Producing sound by breaking up coins

indicators.note: breaking up suggests splitting apart, so the letters of coins are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coins make a noise as they are smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to sound waves, so it describes producing sound.

clue.text: Clay shifting around edge by magic process

indicators.note: around means the rearranged clay letters wrap round the next piece
shifting means the letters of clay move into a new order

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: Moving clay around a rim to perform some wizardry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' makes ALCY from 'Clay', and 'around' puts it round HEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy was the medieval pseudo-science of turning base metal into gold, a seemingly magical transformation.

clue.text: Snake and horse painter

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
RA, Royal Academician, stands for a painter

explanation.surface: An artist paints a snake and a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobra is a venomous snake with a hood.

clue.text: Star takes pay increase at dawn

parts.note: the sun is a star
a rise is British for a pay increase

explanation.surface: A celebrity gets a raise early in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise is the moment the sun appears, which is dawn.

clue.text: Marshland shrub — where? In France

parts.note: bay, the laurel, is a shrub
ou is French for where

explanation.surface: Someone asks where a shrub grows in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayou is a marshy creek or wetland in the southern United States.

clue.text: Very little son isn't able to

parts.note: can't means is not able to

explanation.surface: A son is too weak to manage much at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, so a scant amount is very little.

clue.text: Not quite through, it's almost out of date

indicators.note: not quite means the word for through loses its final letter

parts.note: passed can mean through, as in through an exam or finished

explanation.surface: Someone almost gets through a test, yet the item is nearly expired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's almost' joins the wordplay to the definition, echoing the trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé is a French borrowing meaning old-fashioned, no longer current.
